slides.heading: Dijkstras Algorithm
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Hard · Famous Algorithms
slides.narration: Let's solve Dijkstras Algorithm, a hard famous algorithms problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: Shortest distance from start to every vertex, -1 if unreachable.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. Edges v lists destination, weight (non-negative). Shortest distance from start to every vertex, -1 if unreachable.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Always expand the closest unvisited vertex; with non-negative weights its distance is final.
slides.narration: Always expand the closest unvisited vertex; with non-negative weights its distance is final.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 2. Use a min-heap of distance and vertex
slides.narration: Step by step. First, distances start at infinity. Second, use a min-heap of distance and vertex. Third, relax outgoing edges. Fourth, unreached vertices are minus one.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of (v plus e) log v. Space is O of v.

slides.heading: Recap
bullets: Always expand the closest unvisited vertex; with non-negative weights its distance is final.
